layout.title: What is PAL and MET? Activity Level and Energy Expenditure Explained
layout.intro: PAL (Physical Activity Level) is the activity factor multiplied by BMR to give your TDEE — your actual calorie needs. MET (Metabolic Equivalent of Task) measures how intense a specific activity is relative to rest. Both are used to calculate energy expenditure, but in different ways.

body.text: Choose the right PAL for your calorie goal

The most common mistake in TDEE calculation is overestimating your activity level. If you train 3 days per week but sit still the rest of the day, you are probably "lightly active" (PAL 1.375) — not "moderately active" (PAL 1.55).
A practical method: start with a conservative PAL value and increase if your weight drops faster than planned. It's easier to adjust up than to handle an excessively large calorie deficit.
Try our TDEE calculator to calculate your calorie needs with different activity levels and see how large the difference actually is.

faq.question: What is the difference between PAL and MET?
faq.answer: PAL (Physical Activity Level) is a daily average factor multiplied by BMR to give TDEE. PAL 1.2 = sedentary, PAL 1.9 = extremely active. MET (Metabolic Equivalent of Task) measures energy expenditure for a single activity relative to rest (1 MET = resting energy). PAL is a daily average; MET is activity-specific.

faq.question: How do you choose the right PAL factor?
faq.answer: PAL 1.2 (Sedentary): office work, minimal movement. PAL 1.375 (Lightly active): light exercise 1–3 days/week. PAL 1.55 (Moderately active): exercise 3–5 days/week. PAL 1.725 (Very active): hard training 6–7 days/week. PAL 1.9 (Extremely active): physical work + daily intense training. Choose honestly based on your total weekly activity.

faq.question: Can you calculate TDEE with MET values instead of PAL?
faq.answer: Yes — TDEE = BMR × PAL, or alternatively: sum energy expenditure per activity via MET values (Energy kcal = MET × weight(kg) × time(h)) and add BMR × 24 for resting burn. The MET method is more accurate for specific exercise periods but more complex to apply daily.

faq.question: Why do PAL factors differ between individuals?
faq.answer: NEAT (Non-Exercise Activity Thermogenesis) — unplanned movement like fidgeting, standing, walking — varies enormously (200–800 kcal/day) and significantly affects PAL. Two people with identical exercise routines but different NEAT can have PAL factors differing by 0.2–0.3 units.
